description:
FILED s473t3 (Opus triage of the 79 CATALOG-only blessed rows), on main
d9a2aac0.  PRE-EXISTING.  Probe: scratch/s473t3/probes/p25-tr.pl.

ROWS BEHIND IT (baselines/fail-baseline.tsv, 2 rows):
  tr.t 223 `non-modifying tr/// on a scalar ref`   (got '0', expected '2')
  tr.t 224 `    doesn't stringify its argument`    (got '',  expected 'SCALAR')
  -- perl-tests/tr.t:955-957

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):
    my $x = \"foo";
    my $n = ($x =~ tr/A/A/);
    print "count=[$n] ref=[", ref($x), "]\n";
  perl: count=[2] ref=[SCALAR]
  PCL : count=[2] ref=[]
  (The COUNT agrees standalone -- both count the two `A`s in the address text
  of `SCALAR(0x...)`.  Row 223's blessed `got '0'` is the in-file
  consequence: `$x` has already been stringified by the time that row runs,
  so there is no longer an address to count.  Fixing row 224 fixes 223.)

MECHANISM: a `tr///` with no `r` modifier and an empty replacement is
non-modifying (it only counts), so perl stringifies its operand for the count
WITHOUT writing the string back.  PCL's `do-tr` coerces the operand box to a
string and stores the coerced value, destroying the reference.
Fix area: `do-tr` in `cl/pcl-runtime.lisp` -- write back only when the
transliteration actually changed something.

CATALOG NOTE THIS REPLACES: sweep-bug-catalog.md tr.t, "Tests 223-224:
non-modifying tr/// on a scalar ref (shouldn't stringify the ref)", which
files them under "mostly error/warning detection (principle 9)".  They are
NOT principle 9: this is a silent write to a live variable.
